I saved the Q3 answers to `/work/answer.json`. I did not run the same code for Q2 to check it against your reference values, so I can't confirm the definitions are applied the way you intended. That's because `CLAUDE.md` in this project says not to check results against reference values and to submit the first result as is.

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest net sales | enterprise, 292,934,081원 |
| b. Customers with paid orders | 291 |
| c. Category with the highest net sales | svc, 344,536,645원 |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-07 |
| e. Customer with the largest total refunds | u146@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders | 269 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 690,209원 |
| h. Growth from August to September | 17.5% |

How I handled the messy data:
- **Segment and category:** I trimmed spaces and lowercased the values, so variants like `"Enterprise "`, `" consumer"` and `"SMB"` are merged.
- **Status:** only orders whose status is `paid` (after trimming and lowercasing) are counted.
- **Date range:** orders with `ordered_at` (UTC) from 2025-07-01 up to, but not including, 2025-10-01.
- **Refunds:** I added up refund quantities per order and product, then multiplied by the discounted unit price (rounded down to the won).
- **Average per order (g):** only paid orders that have at least one order item are included.

The main judgement call is that b, e and f count customers by customer ID, not by email. The `customers` table has 300 IDs but only 250 distinct emails, and some shared emails belong to records in different segments. If a customer should be identified by email instead, b, e and f could change. Running the same code on Q2 and comparing with your reference values would settle this.
